summary.headline: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin hit a record 11.90% on INR229.89 crore total income (+19% YoY); order book rose to INR650 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR229.89 crore (+19% YoY), EBITDA INR27.36 crore (+25% YoY) at 11.90% margin, and PAT INR18.45 crore. For FY26, total income was INR825.45 crore (+15%), EBITDA INR93.57 crore (11.34% margin) and PAT INR61.94 crore (+16%). Order book at 31 March 2026 was INR650 crore, up from about INR450 crore at Q3, with the INR200 crore increase entirely from Maruti Suzuki new models. Management declined to give FY27 guidance, instead pointing to a long-term INR3,000 crore revenue ambition for FY30 that is only partly covered by the current order book.

financial_highlights.change: +25% YoY; described as highest ever margin

financial_highlights.metric: ROCE (ex ROU, surplus cash and land)

financial_highlights.change: Revised consolidated cash flow filed 13 May after XBRL filing error
up from about INR450 crore at Q3 FY26; highest in company history

segments.name: Seat covers and frames (NDR Auto)
segments.commentary: NDR does seat covers and frames; Bharat Seats (investee, ~28% held by NDR) does seat assembly and foam. Current revenue run-rate cited as about INR830-850 crore.

segments.name: Hayashi JV (50:50)
segments.commentary: Sunshade business of about INR20 crore transferred to the JV; INR80 crore approved project cost with about INR30 crore invested so far. Production start delayed from April to June due to operational issues. Two small ambient lighting orders from Maruti Suzuki, expected INR10-20 crore revenue combined.

guidance_outlook: No annual guidance given; management pointed to long-term plans. FY30 revenue ambition is INR3,000 crore for NDR standalone (excluding Bharat Seats), implying roughly INR500 crore from existing customers and products plus INR1,000 crore still to be won; updates promised by end of CY2026.

Management said current EBITDA margin (about 11.5% ex other income) is sustainable; gross margin expected to be similar as commodities are indexed. No margin range given for when new products ramp, citing start-up costs.
Bharat Seats FY30 revenue guidance raised to INR3,500 crore from INR3,000 crore (per management, on the Bharat Seats target).
Management said order book adds about INR650 crore to revenue with programs lasting 7-8 years; FY27 growth expected to be similar but no number given.

Capex: about INR150 crore for new product back-end infrastructure (seat inserts, ambient lighting, shades, seat latches, seat belt reminder) on track; another INR30-40 crore general capex plus INR40-50 crore to execute the new order book, over and above the INR150 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR200 crore order book increase from new models or new OEMs, and what caused the Hayashi JV start delay?
qa_highlights.answer: All new Maruti Suzuki models; eVitara removed from the book as it entered production. The JV start moved about two months to June because of operational issues, not capex delay.

qa_highlights.question: Other expenses rose from INR21 crore to INR24 crore QoQ; were there one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-offs; the rise reflects higher project and marketing expenses including R&D.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 11.5% EBITDA margin sustainable, and what margin range applies as new products ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current margin is sustainable and gave no range for the ramp, citing start-up costs.

qa_highlights.question: How much visibility is there to the INR3,000 crore FY30 target?
qa_highlights.answer: INR500 crore is targeted from existing customers and products; the remaining INR1,000 crore needs more time, with an update promised by end of calendar 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order visibility for the INR150 crore new-product capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Seat belt reminder, seat latch and seat insert orders are already held and will move to the new facilities, with production starting January 2027 and ramping slowly. Hayashi has two ambient lighting orders and the shade business.

qa_highlights.question: Why was operating cash flow weak, and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said operating cash flow was positive at INR37.12 crore after a corrected filing on 13 May; about INR12 crore went to a Delhi office, INR6 crore supported subsidiaries and MSME vendor payables rose. Management expects normalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any FY27 revenue or margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No annual guidance; management pointed to the FY30 plan and said some growth is expected in FY27 without a number.

qa_highlights.question: Capex for FY27 and whether the Bharat Seats target changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Another INR30-40 crore general capex plus INR40-50 crore for the new order book, over and above the INR150 crore. Bharat Seats FY30 target raised to INR3,500 crore from INR3,000 crore.

capex_capacity: Capex for new product back-end infrastructure (seat inserts, ambient lighting, shades, seat latches, seat belt reminder) is on track; management said the about INR150 crore plan is ongoing.

Seat insert and seat frame/trim (NDR Auto South) capex largely done; seat latch and seat belt reminder capex still in progress, per management's answer on the project slide (about INR102 crore already spent on listed product lines per analyst).
Additional general capex of INR30-40 crore this year, plus INR40-50 crore to execute the new order book, stated as over and above the INR150 crore.

Hayashi JV: INR80 crore approved project cost, about INR30 crore invested so far (about INR10-15 crore each by the two partners); production start pushed from April to June due to operational issues; investment to be phased with business wins.
Land: 26 acres at Aurangabad and 9 acres at Kharkhoda available for expansion; Toyota-linked Aurangabad expansion under bidding, with plans to replicate the seat business there.
demand_pricing: Order book at 31 March 2026 INR650 crore, up from about INR450 crore at Q3; the INR200 crore increase is entirely new Maruti Suzuki models, with the eVitara order removed as production started.
Management said the order book adds about INR650 crore to revenue over programmes lasting 7-8 years, against current revenue of about INR830-850 crore.
Gross margin up about 100 bps QoQ on normal product mix and vendor volume discounts; management expects gross margin to be similar as commodities are indexed.
Management said the EBITDA margin of about 11.5% excluding other income is sustainable; no margin range given for new product ramp due to start-up costs.
Premiumisation: management expects content per seat to rise about 40-50% over the next 5 years, model to model (artificial leather, power and ventilated seats).
Two small ambient lighting orders from Maruti Suzuki for the Hayashi JV, expected revenue INR10-20 crore combined; sunshade business of about INR20 crore transferred to the JV.
risks_watch: Order book conversion: the INR1,000 crore of the FY30 target remains unidentified, and management will update only by end CY2026.
Concentration: the INR200 crore order-book increase is entirely from Maruti Suzuki, and management confirmed share gains partly come from another supplier losing share.

Hayashi JV utilisation: about INR30 crore invested against INR80 crore approved, with the order book small (INR10-20 crore ambient lighting plus about INR20 crore sunshades) and start delayed to June.
Cash flow: the corrected operating cash flow filing on 13 May 2026 after an XBRL error, and working-capital pressure from MSME vendor payments.
Margin: start-up costs on new products could dilute margins; no range given. Employee costs up about 33% for the year, with management citing hiring for growth.

Watch next quarter: Hayashi JV production start in June, new seat belt reminder, seat latch and seat insert lines starting January 2027, the product mix disclosure promised for the next presentation, and the Aurangabad Toyota-linked bid outcome.
key_quotes: These, I must add, are the highest ever EBITDA margins for NDR Auto.
INR500 crore we want to do from existing customers and our existing products. INR1,000 crore is something I think you will have to give us more time on.
So, the entire INR200 crore is from Maruti Suzuki.
We do not give annual guidance. We have given a four-year, five-year long-term plan guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the order book and margins, but evasive on forward numbers: management gave no FY27 guidance, declined to size the INR1,000 crore FY30 gap, and deferred revenue mix and Bharat Seats capex details. Cautious on new-product margin ramp, citing start-up costs.

growth.why: No annual FY27 guidance given; FY30 standalone revenue ambition of INR3,000 crore (INR1,000 crore not yet visible) backed by an INR650 crore order book (7-8 year programmes) and about INR150 crore plus INR40-50 crore capex, with FY27 growth said to be similar but unquantified.
